assessment.summary: ERBB2 (HER2) is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged oncology targets in human medicine, with 14 approved drugs spanning monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and small-molecule kinase inhibitors. Structural data is exceptionally rich (63 PDB entries, best resolution 1.25Å, multiple ligand-bound structures), and chemical evidence is outstanding (>5,000 IC50 entries, median 301 nM). Literature support is extensive and continuously growing, with strong disease validation across breast, gastric, bladder, colorectal, and other cancers.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 74.0 with only 66.8% high-confidence residues suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular or linker domains) not fully resolved by crystallography — functional relevance of these regions to druggability is not fully characterised
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., HER2 mutations, bypass signalling) remain an active area of investigation and limit durability of current therapies
Emerging indications (bladder, colorectal, liver fibrosis) have less clinical validation compared to breast and gastric cancer
Optimal patient stratification beyond HER2 amplification/overexpression (e.g., HER2-low, HER2-ultralow) is still being defined
Combination therapy strategies and sequencing of approved agents lack definitive consensus in many tumour types
